p: We practice wordlessly today, except at the beginning of the time we spend with God.
ev: Spend fifteen minutes thus when you awake, and gladly give another fifteen more before you go to sleep.
And we will hourly remember Him Who is salvation and deliverance.

p: This day I will accept myself as what my Father's Will created me to be.
ev: We think of truth alone as we arise, and spend five minutes practicing its ways
hourly invite Him with the words with which the day began, concluding it with this same invitation to your Self.

len: five minutes; ten would be better; fifteen better still
ev: Five minutes now becomes the least we give to preparation for a day in which salvation is the only goal we have.
Nor will we willingly give less at night, in gratitude and joy.
At times, perhaps, a minute, even less, will be the most that we can offer as the hour strikes.

p: I am among the ministers of God, and I am grateful that I have the means by which to recognize that I am free.
note: Lesson 153 sets this form: begin each day with at least five minutes, the same at night, and remember the idea as the hour strikes. Lessons after it without their own schedule follow it.

p: I will step back and let Him lead the way, For I would walk along the road to Him.

p: I light the world, I light my mind and all the minds which God created one with me.
ev: This question should be asked a thousand times a day, till certainty has ended doubting and established peace.

p: Select one brother, symbol of the rest, and ask salvation of him.
ev: Today we practice in a form we have attempted earlier.
Be sure you use it instantly, should you be tempted to attack a brother and perceive in him the symbol of your fear.
r: I would behold you with the eyes of Christ, and see my perfect sinlessness in you.

ev: arising with them in his mind, recalling them throughout the day, at night bringing them with him as he goes to sleep.
